title: Separator Search Halting Result
statement: Let $C,e,B,p$ be natural numbers, let $	ext{mode}$ be a Boolean flag, let $f$ map finite Boolean words to finite Boolean words, and let $x,b$ be finite Boolean words. Let $v$ assign a natural number to each of $14$ registers. Suppose every register value is at most $B$, register $3$ equals twice the length of the pairing of $x$ with $b$, register $4$ equals $4|x|+4$, register $13$ equals twice the length of $f(x)$, register $5$ equals $p$, twice the length of $f(x)$ is at most $p$, and the length of the pairing of $f(x)$ with $b$ is at most $B$. Starting in the separator state with flag false and with no answer recorded, the machine halts with answer $p<|�\langle f(x),b\rangle|$ if $	ext{mode}$ is true, and otherwise with the bit at position $p$ of $�\langle f(x),b\rangle$, taking the bit to be false when $p$ is beyond its length. Every configuration before halting satisfies the program's step-validity condition and has all register values at most $B$.

replaced:
Let $C,e,B,p$ be natural numbers, let $\mathrm{mode}$ be a Boolean flag, let $f$ map bit
strings to bit strings, and let $x,b$ be bit strings. Suppose $v$ assigns a natural
number to each of the 14 registers, every register value is at most $B$, register $3$
equals twice the length of the encoding of $x$ paired with $b$, register $4$ equals
$4|x|+4$, register $13$ equals twice the length of $f(x)$, register $5$ equals $p$,
twice the length of $f(x)$ is at most $p$, and the length of the encoding of $f(x)$
paired with $b$ is at most $B$. Starting in the separator-search state with its first
phase flag false, the specified counter machine halts with the answer that is true
exactly when $p$ is less than that encoded length if $\mathrm{mode}$ is true; otherwise
its answer is the bit at position $p$ of the encoding, using false when that position is
beyond the end. Throughout the run, the machine's step-validity condition holds and
every register remains at most $B$.
